a-romance-of-billy-goat-hill: Alice Hegan Rice — beloved author of Mrs. Wiggs of the Cabbage Patch — sets this romance on Billy-Goat Hill, where a poor but proud Kentucky family guards its dignity. A young woman's heart and a neighborhood's prejudices collide in a story full of local color. Rice's affection for her characters shines on every page.
wilhelm-tell: Schiller's beloved drama tells of William Tell, the Swiss marksman forced to shoot an apple from his son's head, and the uprising his defiance inspires. Freedom, tyranny, and the Alps themselves fill this stirring play. Performed ever since 1804, it remains the classic drama of liberty.
the-coming-of-bill: Wodehouse's comedy turns on Bill — a baby whose arrival upends the lives, romances, and ambitions of the adults around him. Custody battles and love affairs tangle in the author's inimitable style. A lesser-known Wodehouse, but pure delight for his fans.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-st-g: A 1913 entry on St. Gall, the Swiss abbey of the famous plan and library. Irish Gall's hermitage grew great. George Cyprian Alston details its riches. The most learned house of the Alps. Notker the Stammerer sang his sequences in its choir.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albert-knoll: A 1913 entry on Albert Knoll — the Capuchin dogmatic theologian. Stephen Donovan praises his textbooks. Seminaries learned doctrine from his pages. His Institutiones ran to many editions. A friar among the doctors. His moral theology guided the confessors. His works crossed the Alps in translation.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-mac: A 1913 entry on Alexander MacDonell — the Bishop of Kingston, father of Glengarry. Donald MacDonald honors his pioneer zeal. He led his Highlanders to Canada. The wilderness became a diocese. A bishop of the backwoods. His regiment fought in the Napoleonic wars.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-bell: This 1913 reference piece on the altar bell — the Sanctus bell of the Mass. Augustin Schulte describes its use. Its tinkle marks the consecration. The faithful lift their hearts at the sound. The Mass's silver voice. Its ring still stirs the children's awe.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-angelus-bell: This 1913 reference article on the Angelus bell — the thrice-daily call to prayer. Herbert Thurston traces its history. Morning, noon, and evening answer. The fields paused at its sound. The day's threefold summons. Its bronze has rung for centuries. Its peal still marks the hours.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arthur-bell: A 1913 entry on Arthur Bell — the Franciscan martyr of England. Stephen Donovan honors his death. He died for the old faith's sake. The entry preserves his modest fame. A friar of the English martyrs. His death honored the Franciscan habit.
